translation_variants_and_conflicts.summary: Cheiro reads it as caution and low self-confidence; Benham as reliance on others; Heron-Allen as the favourable norm of good sense and strength of will. The synthesis must show all three.
Iyer 1884 reads three lines rising to mid-palm; Zysk 2016/2025 and Hastasanjivana vv. 39-41 read three wrist bracelets. Keep both readings until the Sanskrit reviewer rules.

crosswalk.note: No Indian counterpart in I1; check I2 later
Both value deep, clear lines, but I1 reads all palm lines together while the Western schools read each line separately; agreement can only be claimed at the 'general line quality' level
Tempting to equate the two; NOT allowed until a source supports it

crosswalk.b: W.finger proportions (Cheiro Part II ch. III)

crosswalk.relation: positional match, NOT an equivalence of meaning
crosswalk.note: Same crease, different names and meanings (Zysk 2025 p. 244). The UI must not translate 'ayu rekha' as 'life line'.

renderings.text: If the three lines issuing from the wrist reach the middle of the palm, the person will be a king
a king is the man who has three lines on the wrist
